newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing-no reason to expect key rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing-no reason to expect key rate cuts.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Wednesday there was no reason to expect further reductions in key German interest rates and that the German economy was performing better than expected.
In an interview with German television, Issing said : "Key rates are at a historic low and here, nothing more is to be expected or necessary."

Issing added that Germany's economy was gaining momentum.

"The economy has improved markedly since the spring, although not spectacularly. The end-of-year result should be better than was expected at the start of the year," Issing said in an interview with the ZDF television channel.
Issing said the economy was being underpinned by moderate wage rises this year, increasing consumer confidence following tax cuts at the start of the year and calmer foreign exchange markets.
"We're not out of the woods yet," Issing said. But the basis was there to believe that the upswing would continue into next year.
The key to ensure lasting economic growth was to boost investment, which had been lagging, Issing said.
He added that investment would have to increase to ensure a lasting recovery. In addition, the tax burden was too high at present to be compatible with stable economic growth in the long term.
